title: 1906 Tolls were removed, the bridge became free
description: This zoomed-in photo from Buddy Barss’s collection showcases the toll booth on the east end of the uncovered bridge. Right from the start, residents grumbled about the tolls and doubted they would last. Many locals found ways to avoid paying, such as using an ice bridge during winter. In response, the bridge directors lowered prices, stopped charging pedestrians and funeral processions, and only collected tolls during certain hours. The fees were meant to cover maintenance and pay the toll gatekeeper, but harsh weather rapidly deteriorated the wooden structure, and toll revenue proved inadequate. Tolls continued until 1906, when a government election promised to eliminate them and assume responsibility for maintenance. There was no fanfare or official announcement; one day, the toll gatekeeper, James Pearson, simply didn’t show up for work. (Photo courtesy of  Buddy Barss)
